newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarussian deputies allow foreigners to buy land.
newsitem.headline: Belarussian deputies allow foreigners to buy land.

text.p: The Belarussian parliament on Wednesday passed land law amendments proposed by President Alexander Lukashenko allowing foreigners to own land in the former Soviet republic.

"Foreign legal entities now can buy land on the same basis as Belarussian ones," Anatoly Belogurov, a member of parliament's agrarian committee, told Reuters, adding lands made available for private sale would be increased.
The amendments do not exclude the right by foreign investors to lease land for 99 years.
The move seems a reversal by Lukashenko, who last November won a referendum with a question on private ownership on land. The majority of voters rejected the idea then.
Belogurov said foreign companies and the Belarussian government would negotiate a specific price for land in each case, but the final say on a price would belong to the president.
